text:
You are the student of a powerful necromancer. He has been training you for most of your life in the arts he has mastered. He is old now and relies greatly upon your youthfulness.

Just before the crowning moment of his life's work, a band of murderhobos had broken into his tower and murdered him. He told you to flee, so that you may live. You gathered up the most prized books in the necromancer's collection, managing to sneak out of the tower and flee into the night.

name: Gods

options.label: The Mother
options.description: She is the light that shines, illuminating the world and giving life to all. She loves her children very much, and does not want to see harm come to them. This has lead to her church passing restrictive laws to enforce safety upon all. Additionally, her people have come to rely upon The Mother for a great many things. The Mother does not wish her children to stay among the living or too long as she wishes to embrace them after a full life. Because of this, using magic to extend one's life is seen as "abandoning the Mother" and her chuch has a whole order dedicating to stamping out this heresy. Creating life from unlife is also frowned upon, as only the Mother is seen as having the right to create life. As such the creation of life is her domain.

options.label: The Father
options.description: The Father, also called the Dark Lord. He is the most common god for those that do not worship the Mother for her restrictive views of what is to be. His philosophy elevates the strong, and the gifts that he gives always come with a price. People that worship the Father tend to value strength, individual skills, and adherence to duty. The Father does not intefere in the lives of his followers, but will answer certain prayers. The Father is often criticized for appearing to be absent in the world, but her merely wishes his followers and all the people of the world to rise and fall upon their own merits. If his people are in need of him, he will help them though. His symbol holds great power and there are orders that use it to conquer their enemies; though whether they succeed or not is up to them.

options.label: The Child
options.description: The Child is neither boy nor girl. It is both yet neither. Aggressive tactics were commonplace and the Child itself wished for its people to rule the world, and have all the room they needed for their rapidly growing population, and its people reflected this. The Parents benaished it beneath the southern-most continent, where it sleeps. The Child has become much more caring in its rest, slowly undoing the damage it has wrought. Thus, the Child has a split personality that embodies the virtues of both the Mother and the Father. The Child now gives aid to its worshipers, but without as many restrictions on behavior, action or such.

options.label: None
options.description: Some people in the world have decided that the gods are not deserving of worship and have chosen to serve themselves. They pay no heed to the gods and their wills. They must rely on their own skills. Operating on their own or in small cults and organizations, those that do not worship the gods draw upon the force that permeates the world around them. Most often, they will use symbols and seals to tap into the magic of the world and may not even have any intrinsic power themselves. The oldest and most powerful organization of the non-worshipers is the Necropolis, a group of liches dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge for its own sake.

description:
There are three gods that rule the world. 

Most people worship them. 

Which one do you worship?

name: Race

options.label: Elves
options.description:
The elves inhabit the ancestral home of the elven people, and all of them worship the Father. The representative of the Father in this world is the high priest called the Holy King Representative of the Dark Father, shortened to the King for brevity. 

The King is the head of a patriarchal government installed by an earlier king. 

Their long lives reduce the need for reproduction, privileging the individual further. 

Despite having agriculture, the elves maintain a strong hunting tradition, with hunting as a rite of passage for the transition to adulthood. This rite uses a thrown spear to kill an animal in a single strike, with the spear and animal left as an offering to the Father. A child or adult that has not completed this is said to "have their spear" and the term is often used in a derogatory manner. Elves enjoy hunting and will often foray far into Teb'Hai and the Untamed Lands for slaves, chattel, and livestock. This is seen as their right as elves. 

The elves have a system of aggressive displays to determine hierarchy, with only the most worthy able to remain in power for any period of time. 

The artistoracy of the elves are called the Fair Ones, and have deathly pale skin. The Fair Ones are immortal and undead, having claimed the right to lead from the Father. The first and best gift the elves ever received was their hunting rites. By performing the correct ritual while hunting, the elve ensure the unspent life force from their kill is transferred directly to the,, extending their life by days, months, or even years at a time. depending upon the qualities of the quarry.

options.label: Humans
options.description:
Humans are the most populous of the races, and were crafted by the Mother as the perfect beings to love. Humans tend to worship the Mother, They are. used to her buiding hand, and have formed a martriarchal society in her image. 

They were crafted in the image of the elves, but made softer and kinder, even good. 

Thus humans linger for only a century, and are driven to do much more than any elf. 

They have two kingdoms: Teb'lhr and Teb'Ris. With Teb'lhr's southern region on the border of Zatmenyir the humans are a prime target for the Dark Elf slave hunting parties, and thus have formed tightly-woven communities with strong walls. 

Teb'lhrans were the first humans, and adapated to their desert-bound home well, with the biggest cities springing up in the lush green areas of the North-West. Clinging close to Mount Gurinta, which reminds them of the Mother. They have developed skin of all shades, pale, gold, and bronze, with the desert-dwellers having skin with midnight hue. They have come to rely upon the Mother for the resources they need, and she has provided for them thus far. They have a love for golden jewelry and the finest fabrics they can get. The heat of Teb'lhr had led to them wearing very little clothing.

Teb'Risians have lost the ebon skin of their forefathers, and found the many green forested areas much better than their original homeland. They have a love for bright colors, but the land lacks much in the way of dyes. Worshiping the Father as an equal to the Mother, they were exiled for attempting to bring this equality to Teb'lhr. 

Less socially and legally strict, the Teb'Risians are more permissive of activities that both the elves and Teb'lhrans find abhorrent.

options.label: Kobolds
options.description:
Kobolds were the first truly original creation by the Child, and worship it as their one true god. Kobolds live a life of simplicity, free from worry and trouble, They want for nothing of the physical realm. Kobolds have very few possessions, and kobold in all societies all things belong to everyone and no-one simultaenously. Kobolds follow an ascetic lifestyle that aids them in releasing their burden in life. 

The kobolds typically live in the desert of the Untamed Lands, but are known to have immigrated to other nations. Here, they have spread their philosophy of life with those longer-lived than them. Kobolds believe the Child has two sides: A masculine side when it is awake that causes great and terrible events, and a feminine side when it is asleep that helps and heals the sick and wounded. 

Even more populous than the humans, the Kobolds have the shortest life expentency and the greatest rate of repoduction. Kobolds tend to live for up to half a century, and have dozens of children in this time, having reached adulthood after 5 years. They have scaly, reptilian visage and look very much alike a humanoid lizard. 

Kobolds are a cold-blooded people, and thrive in warm lands, They are half the height of man and elf, but are able to keep their memories through the cycle of life. 

Kobolds are prime targets for the Dark Elves' slave hunting parties and have a large slave population in Zatmenyir, due to their great ability to perform manual labor and tasks.

description: There are 3 sentient races in the world, with many other non-sentient races. Which sentient race are you?

subcategories.name: Country
subcategories.text:
There are many countries in the world. 

To which do you flee?

options.label: Koudeis
options.description: The Northlands: It is home to few living things other than trees. Covered in ice and snow, sentient undead have taken up residence in this nation due to cold, isolation, and inhospitibility to the living. The scarcity of life means there is no capital of Koudeis.

options.label: Teb'lhr
options.description: The ancient lands: It was the first place that the Gods talked to poeple at Mount Gurinta millennia ago. It has a large desert with countless ruins in its sands as people come and go with the wind. To the south is a lush land full of plains, forests, and potential.

options.label: Teb'Ris
options.description: When a failed coup in Teb'lhr lead to the exile of the traitors to what seemed like a desert land, the exiles thrived. Its people worship both the Parents, which was the reason for both the coup and exile. Teb'Ris has become a powerful but young nation.

options.label: Zatmenyir
options.description:
The first nation of elves: The forest is their birthright. 

Zatmenyir's borders extend to the horizon around their sacred forest, but no further. 

With mighty skyscrapers formed around and inside massive trees, those that trespass rarely return.

options.label: Valaistir
options.description: The second nation of elves: They migrated to the land across the pond. This separation has changed them: These elves have delved into creating building out of other things than trees and the lack of a heavy forest has necessitated warmer, more concealing clothes.

options.label: The Untamed Lands
options.description: Neither human nor elf has recognized the legitimacy of any kingdom within these lands. It is the home of the lizard-like race called the Kobolds. While there are many cities and flourishing communities, the land is home to the Child, which will forever tarnish its name.

options.label: Teb'Ris City
options.description: The city is prosperous with over a hundred thousand souls within. Most ideas have been pursued here, with nearly all scholars from Teb'Ris having studied here. They may even be those sympathetic to your cause.

options.label: Teb'Ris Capital
options.description: Close to the desert where the exiles wondered for 30 days, it sits on the coast and more than million souls call it home. Homes are always for sale here and discreet citizens can get away with almost anything.

options.label: Zatmenyir Small Tree Town
options.description: A series of interconnected trees with structures all along their lengths housing elven families. All members of the town hunt. The canopy hides sunlight, with only twilight at the best of times.

options.label: Zatmenyir Tree Town
options.description: A series of trees, which house over give hundred elves. Homes are carved into the still-living trees, a sort of civilized society exists here, with slaves supporting the elven lifestyle. Agriculture has taken off here.

options.label: Zatmenyir Tree City
options.description: Thick trees, interwoven branches and great height, this city has existed for millennia. The elves operate the slave market for the smaller cities and almost anything or anyone can be bought here.

options.label: Zatmenyir Capital
options.description: Set on the coast of the great lake of Zatmenyir, it has over a million elves in residence with the largest slave market in the land. It is also the most racially tolerant of all elven cities. Most elves only go on annual hunts.

options.label: Valaistir Town
options.description: Located in the forests near Saliin are a great number of building constructed from wood and stone. The elves here have formed a community with a much softer lifestyle than their mainland cousins.

options.label: Valaistir Tree City
options.description: Within a series of large trees, surrounded by forest and dense greenery. Most like the homeland, it has continued the traditions of building homes inside trees and of hunting, though slaves are imported.

options.label: Saliin
options.description: Situated atop a fountain of magic energy, the paved streets glow with magic. Citizens have enjoyed great magical prowess. Saliin has a distinct lack of slaves, instead employing magically created servants.

options.label: Valaistir Capital
options.description: A blend of buildings and greenery, with astounding spires and slender bridges. The elves here import most of their slaves and food. The elven lifestyle here has little in common with that of the mainland elves.

options.label: Desert City
options.description: Breathtaking vistas of seas of sand and dunes as far as the eye can see. Bazaars and trading posts are the lifeblood of the city, and people from all over the Untamed Lands can be found here.

options.label: Overgrown Ruins
options.description: Sprawling stone structures, perfectly preserved and overgrown, it was built many centuries ago. The doorway seems small for a human, but the chambers have high ceilings.

options.label: Hollow Mountain Lair
options.description: Hollowed out rooms connected by tunnels, it has its fair share of entrances and exits. A sparse few people still live in it, but they tend to be hiding from someone, or something. The land around is mostly inhospitable.

options.label: Untamed Lands Capital
options.description: Defying the reputation forced upon them, the Lands have a city that is awe-inspiring as the rest of the world. The inhabitants of the capital are mostly kobolds, but humans are a large minority here.

options.label: Rocky Mountain Fortress
options.description: Hidden in the mountain, the majority of it lies beneath the ground. There is an armory somewhere, and even a barracks that can house many. It guarded an important place, but times have changed.

options.label: Cliffside Settlement
options.description: Carved directly into the side of a cliff is a community of free kobolds. The people are not willing to go back to a life of slavery, but if pressed may return. The settlement is remarkably cool inside.

options.label: Desert Fortress
options.description: Established as a fortress-town in a strategically important location, it has a small militia garrison. Hardy people, they can go without food and water from caravans for a surprisingly long time.

options.label: Necromancer's Lair
options.description: A long-forgotten necromancer had constructed a grand lair, but over the centuries of neglect it has fallen into a decrepit state, with signs of disrepair abundant. It will be in need of repairs.

options.label: City Sewers
options.description: Beneath a city somewhere there exists an extensive networks of sewers. It smells and is remarkably filthy, but no one who considers themselves respectable will willingly enter the sewers to look for anything.

options.label: Roadside Inn
options.description: By the side of a road, it is cloaked in a dark miasma which drives people to seek shelter. The previous owner has kept up a good reputation and provides a good service, with room and board and a hot meal. The visitors will not ask many questions.

options.label: Serene Village
options.description: In a small and oft-ignored corner of the nation, it has gotten by without any slave raids or other strike in its past. Everyone knows everyone, and though outsiders are rare, any outsiders may be welcomed.

options.label: Mountaintop Mansion
options.description: Carefully placed to be the most impressive of all mansions, it has over a hundred rooms and can be reached via a small bridge connecting the mansion to a cliffside tower.

options.label: Underground Shrine
options.description:
One of the caves you have found has led to you a secret place of worship for a cult. 

It may be that they worshiped the Child, or even the Father. It is dark and damp, with streams throughout.

options.label: Cave
options.description:
Little more than a hole in the side of a mountain, it has little in the way of comfort, but few visitors. 

With a little work, you may shape it into a fine home. 

There even appears to be some old mine shafts.

options.label: Burial Tomb
options.description: A mound of stone that houses the entrance to the tomb of a local village. Established to give the dead an honorable resting place, their last caregiver has taken up residency and a replacement is needed.

options.label: Twilight Isles Fortification
options.description: Located on a tropical beach on the coast of the Twilight Isles, established as an elven military outpost, it had exchanged hands more times than can be remembered. No living soul occupies the fortification.

options.label: Forest Home
options.description: An out-of-the-way house in the forest. It's previous owner sold it after their last relative moved away. The home had fallen into a slight state of disrepair, but the small farm adjacent has always provided food for the home, and can do so once again. The home has a cosy feel to it, and there is a nearby village.

options.label: Ghost Town
options.description: Somewhere in one of the nations lies a town abandoned. It is said that the restless spirits of the dead wander its streets left behind by a spiritualist. It may be that they were caught unawares, but they are long gone. Few but spirits reside here, but a necromancer may be able to control them once again.

options.label: The Lonely Tower
options.description: Erected by one that valued their privacy, it overlooks an expanse of nothing on the edge of the cliff. Few have heard of it and even fewer have laid eyes on it, but the guide shows you the way there. The land is in a perpetual state of gloom chocked by a miasma of despair, yet it is perfect for dark works of sorcery.

options.label: The Leaning Tower
options.description: The last vestiges of a forgotten mage: It has been considered very unsafe since the angle to which it leans is rather severe. Not many risk entering the tower even with the trove of knowledge and the potential treasures that reside. Bewares the dangers that are both within, and without.

options.label: Forgotten Laboratory
options.description: A bastion of academic and scientific advancement long since left to nature, there are still rooms within that contain untouched works of wonder. Claiming these wonders for yourself will vastly advance your skills, or enhance your creations. With some work, the majority of the laboratory will be in working order.

options.label: Ruins
options.description: They look to be the remnants of a place much older than the trees nearby, and in much worse condition. The ruins look to be open to the air with nary a set of walls between them. You will be sleeping under the stars until you set up some sort of shelter, but there looks to be some clues as to why it was abandoned.

options.label: Abandoned Fortress
options.description: A great castle of stone and iron, it has stood against many forces and prevailed. It may have been rendered obsolete when borders shifted and it was no longer in such a strategic position, or it may have been rendered inhabitable by some dark sorcery, the record does not specify what. All that remains is a sordid legacy.

options.label: Island Castle
options.description: Opulence and sophistication permeate the walls here, for it was not built for battle but instead for pleasure. No expense was spared in its construction and it shows, with masterfully crafted stoneworks and carpentry throughout. It comes with a household staff left behind by the previous owner.

options.label: Ramshackle Town Inn
options.description: A rundown inn that has seen better days. It is located in a rather populated city. The inn is up for sale with a low price, and a cursory inspection of the rooms inside will tell you why. It has great potential but will take a great deal of work to reach that, afterwards it would be a quality inn located in the city.

options.label: Isolated Mansion
options.description: Situated in a remote location with only a sturdy stone bridge for access to the outside world. It is large and spacious, with more rooms that you use, and a ballroom. The one that sold it has informed you that they are not quite sure why the last owners have left, but you are certain you can find out why.

options.label: Traveling Caravan
options.description: Some people prefer to not be tied down. They move from place to place in a small community of their own. Beholden to no one but the Gods, they often act as courtiers, or traveling circuses. As one of these people, you will not stay in one place for too long, and will often need to move packages swiftly.

options.label: Vagrant
options.description: Traveling around with very little to tie you down, you may go from place to place freely. With no place to call your own, you may frequently stay in inns, as you will always be on the move. You are incredibly hard to track and even harder to find, as long as you play it smart.

options.label: Normal Path
options.description: Choose 10 spells: You may choose one from Tier 1

options.label: Mother's Path
options.description:
You may instead desire no more life than what the mother gave you. This frees up much more of your lifetime spent studying. 

Choose 14 spells, but none from Tier 1

subcategories.name: Liber Mortis
subcategories.text: The very first book of necromancy from which all others are derived. The first written by humans: It contains rituals, secrets, and techniques for raising the dead from their rest and controlling their actions.

subcategories.name: Tier 4
subcategories.text: These are the staple skills of any necromancer.

options.label: Create undead
options.description: This spell allows the caster to raise one that has died as a member of the undead, no longer alive but still walking amongst the living. They have all the strength and physical ability they had possessed when alive, however they lack any intelligence. They will decay t the same rate as any other of the dead.

options.label: Ward Undead
options.description:
Acting as a magical barrier to those that were raised to again walk with the living, this spell creates a necromantic shield through which none of the unliving can pass. 

Any room, door, or marked space that this spell is cast upon shall reflect the unliving, though when cast in the open shall only make them recoil.

options.label: Detect Undead
options.description:
A ritual that when performed will grant knowledge about the locations of. any nearby undead. 

Accurate enough to identify them inside a room, it can also provide a direction and a population count.

The after-effect of casting this spell lets the caster "see" the outlines of undead through solid objects: Up to 10km away

options.label: Repel Animal
options.description:
The unnatural origin of the necromantic energies in necromancy, this spell allows the caster to cause animals to flee in terror until the effects wear off. 

This is determined by both the caster and the spell's strength.

Not actually causing harm, it is used when a dangerous animal needs to be dealt with.

options.label: Command Undead
options.description:
While almost all undead are mindless, they are not inherently under your direct control. They would turn on you as soon as anyone else. 

This ability causes any undead you raise to serve you, follow your commands, and do you bidding. 

This ability persists whilst you sleep, but cannot command another's undead.

options.label: Invisibility to Undead
options.description:
A useful spell, it allows the caster to hide in plain sight for any target they wish. Any and all undead will be unable to see the target, but they may still hear and feel them; however, they still will   not be able to see the target.

This spell affects indiscriminately all undead, even your own, and will only affect a single target.

subcategories.name: Tier 3
subcategories.text: These skills are a necromancer's main skills.

options.label: Ray of Enfeeblement
options.description:
Bringing the target nearer to death for a short time, this spell causes the target to become weak and sickly. 

A target affected by this spell may become winded after only a few dozen steps, while finding running impossible. By draining the strength of the caster, they may empower this spell to cause paralysis, while weakening themselves.

options.label: Feign Death
options.description:
A spell used to disguise the living, it can fool all but the most perceptive of people, tricking their senses and making them fully believe the target is dead. 

The pulse and breathing of the target are unable to be felt, though spells can break through this deception. 

The spell can also paralyze the target for a set duration chosen by the caster.

options.label: Create Death Knight
options.description:
A spell that creates an undead creature from a being that was a skilled warrior in life. It commands great martial prowess and experience in battle. 

Typically clad in armor and armed with its favor weapon in life, they have retained their intelligence but must submit to their creator, following them with undying loyalty.

options.label: Disguise Undead
options.description:
Used to pass off the dead as the living, this spell can hide the stench of decay and mask the visage of death. 

Being affected by this spell look and smell exactly like the living, though it does not give them the ability to speak nor can it make them act like the living. 

Useful is the caster wishes to keep undead servants among the living.

options.label: Vision of Death
options.description:
Cast upon a target, this spell shows them a sight of utter horror; their own death.

While not being the exact method by which they will die, it is likely to happen and if the caster knows how they will die, it can be very real.

Affecting more than one target reduces the believeability of the spell.

options.label: Suspended Animation
options.description:
Powered by necromantic energies, this spell can place a living or dead being into a stasis. During this, the target will not age, rot or decay, nor be affected by any ailments that plague them. 

Breathing and other bodily functions will be put on hold as well. 

To the being in stasis, time will seem to pause for them.

subcategories.name: Tier 2
subcategories.text: These are the best skills that a necromancer has learnt.

options.label: Create Lesser Lich
options.description:
Serving as the overseer of the lichdom ritual, you assist a companion in turning into a lich. Their transformation guided by your hand, you help set out of the spells and sigils. 

Your companion's soul is transferred to their phylcatery and they drink their poison.

They rise as a new lich in your service.

options.label: Touch of Death
options.description:
Only able to be cast on contact with a living being, this spell will cause the death of the target when cast. Typically death is from an induced heart attack or anueurism, but the death can take the form of any near-immediate death that requires no outside force. 

This spell cannot cause a suicide.

options.label: Create Greater Undead
options.description:
Far greater in strength than common undead, this spell creates an unliving thing that is much bigger and more powerful than anything a necromancer will usually employ. 

They have the strength of many men and possess great intelligence for an undead, able to execute more than one command, or a string of commands.

options.label: Enhance Undead
options.description:
A spell that improves an undead being that currently exists, making it hardier, stronger, and faster.

It may become grotesque and bigger in size, but the undead cannot be made more intelligent.

If multiple Enhanced undead are in an area, they can communicate simple ideas to each other, such as intruders.

options.label: Create Mass Undead
options.description: Will all undead creations formed one at a time, an army is a laborious process. This spell allows the caster to raise a large number of undead at a a time. Up to 10 undead can be raised each time this spell is cast without penalty, but if more than 10 are raised at once, then all the undead are 10% weaker for every additional 10 undead raised.

options.label: Death Ward
options.description:
This spell is cast in a place or on an item such as a door or a book, and can also be keyed to ignore certain people. Anyone not keyed to be ignored will suffer an instant death from an aneurysm or induced heart attack, or any other means of near-immediate death that needs no outside force. 

This spell cannot cause a suicide.

subcategories.name: Tier 1
subcategories.text:
In persuit of immortality, the necromancer has mastered this. 

Pick 1 spell from this tier.

options.label: Lichdom
options.description:
Found in the texts you saved from your master's library is the way to immortality necromancers tend to pursue. 

Requiring that you sever the connection of soul from your body and place it within a phylcatery, they are thusforth immortal in their undeath, and it makes the lich able to regenerate their body from any damage while it is intact. Any damage or rot that occurs naturally or acccidentally, such as papercuts or rot, are not affected; though broken bones and burns are.

options.label: Totenherrn
options.description: While you saved your masters books, you felt you should have stayed behind. After much sparring and study, you had discovered a ritual that would grant you immortality. You perform the ritual, and you perform the last step, stabbing yourself in the heart with a sword. This kills you, while the spells raise you as a servant in the service of the caster: you. This ritual enhances your strength, durability, reflexes, and immunity to spells that control the dead. Severe physical or holy damage will destroy a Totenherrn.

subcategories.name: Liber Animas
subcategories.text: Written in magic and bound with the soul of a sacrifice, this grimoire contains the knowledge to bind souls and spirits to your will. The sacrifice is bound to serve you and may appear in a spectral form.

subcategories.name: Tier 4
subcategories.text: These are the staple skills of any necromancer

options.label: Speak with the Dead
options.description:
This pet is often a sign that a person has necromantic potential and may happen without deliberately being cast. When deliberately cast, a specific soul can be communicated with.

The castor will hear their voice, or they may choose to talk with a soul that may have information on a topic. Mages of all kinds do not like being called up like this

options.label: Summon Spirits
options.description:
Ritual that calls to the caster a number of spirits from the afterlife. 

The castor must be specific about what spirits can be called by this ritual, last any spirit that wishes answers the call. Not all spirits that answer are friendly. Common summon such as "ancestors" or any other specific group to which a spirit can belong work best.

options.label: Command Spirit
options.description: Any spirit that the caster finds about can be forced to do their will. Usually cast upon malevolent entities, causing harm rather than benevolent ghost seeking peace, this spell compels the spirit to carry out the command and last for a single order, expiring once it is completed.

options.label: Create Ghost
options.description:
Taking the spirit of a recently-deceased person or the soul of a still-living being, the caster can impart into the spirit an unwillingness to move onto the next life. They may also indenture the spirit into their service, and cause them to do their bidding. 

These ghosts can only interact with the world if they wish to do so.

options.label: Spirit Ward
options.description:
By casting this spell in a place the caster causes ward to be placed that will drive away any spirit or ghost that seeks to enter into it. 

While it cannot remove any spirits that already reside in the place, it prevents more from joining them. 

Even one that is Astral Projecting will find themselves barred from entry.

options.label: Craft Soulflask
options.description:
The Liber Animas has a set of plans that outline the creation of a glass flask that can hold a single soul that has been removed from a body, or an item. Loose souls nearby will feel drawn into the flash while it is open.

The soulflask is enchanted to trap the spirit within and prevent them escaping as long as the cap is on.

subcategories.name: Tier 3
subcategories.text: These skills are a necromancer's main skills.

options.label: Trap Soul
options.description:
This spell of the Liber Animas allows the caster to instill a consciousness into an object, such as a weapon, by trapping a soul within it. 

These souls may imbue the object with power and can even be allowed to move or manipulate the object on their own. The souls will know intimately  secrets of the object while within.

options.label: Astral Projection
options.description:
The ritual that frees the soul to wander the world and return safely back to their body. The souls of other projectors as well as the dead that wander the world can be interacted with while projecting. 

The projected soul cannot interact with the world, but neither ca n they be trapped or constrained by the physical world. Gravity also has no hold on them.

options.label: Astral Protection
options.description:
Commonly paired with astral projection, this spell shields a spirit or soul from spells or rituals that would directly affect it. Souls cannot be ripped from a person protected with this spell, nor can those that wander be kidnapped. 

This spell lasts a week, though if cast upon an object will last until removed while the object protects the holder.

options.label: Circle of Bones
options.description:
Constructed from bones, this circle is used in a ritual of communication across vast distances.

By calling a spirit into this circle, a caster can communicate with another circle, through the spirit. The circle at the other end and the caster will both be able to hear each other, but after the call is ended the spirit will depart.

options.label: Undying Servitude
options.description:
This spells binds a spirit within a corpse or a skeleton and enslaves them to the will of the caster. 

The newly-enslaved spirit has magically enhanced strength and the endurance of the undead, and can only be freed by the spell being lifted or their body being destroyed. 

The spirit cannot disobey their master.

options.label: Exorcism
options.description:
The method by which unwanted spirits and ghosts can be forcibly expelled from a person or place, this ritual can be dangerous if performed improperly. By casting holy water and reciting the ritual's spell, the exorcist can drive any unwanted spirits.

No malevolent spirit or ghost can enter the exorcised place for a month.

subcategories.name: Tier 2
subcategories.text: These are the best skills that a necromancer has learnt.

options.label: Craft Soulwell
options.description: The Liber Anomas has a set of plans for the construction of a Soulwell, which is able to hold souls as an unevaporable liquid. The well can be the size of a bowl up to a full-sized well, a cistern or even a dam. The larger well require more effort to construct, and must be made specifically as a soulwell, not converted. The souls each fill a standard-sized cup.

options.label: Create Greater Ghost
options.description: A ritual that is cast over a dying person that transforms their soul into a being with great power, bound to serve you. With their mind intact and their body discarded, they are yours to command. Able to interact with the physical world, and unable to be affected by the physical objects.

options.label: Sever Soul
options.description:
A spell that causes great distress with the body being left bereft of its soul. The soul is then left unanchored to the material world, and may be captured. Such a soul retains the ability to use their senses, though they cannot touch the physical world.

Most likely the target of this spell will be very angry at the caster, so take care.

options.label: Extract Soul
options.description:
Often a soul that has been trapped in an item may wish to be freed, or it may be necessary to remove them. 

This spell allows the caster to forcibly separate a soul from the object they reside in, setting them loose. 

Any object that was powered by or granted powers by the soul inside it will lose these powers.

options.label: Memories of the Soul
options.description:
The Liber Animas has a spell that can be cast upon a pool containing souls, such as a soulwell, that can give the caster a look into the memories of the souls contained within. 

Souls that have passed may also be called into the pool temporarily to lend their memories to the pool so that the caster may experience them.

options.label: Create Soulstone
options.description: Used to enhance a ritual or spell's power by consuming part or all of the soulstone. The soulstone is forged from the crystallization of souls, either a single soul or multiple together, into an ice blue rounded crystal equal in mass to the number of souls that were used to create it. The sole grants a 5% boost in spellpower per soul consumed.

subcategories.name: Tier 1
subcategories.text:
In pursuit of immortality, the necromancer has mastered this.

Pick 1 spell from this tier.

options.label: Soul Drinker
options.description:
While the instructions to build a Soul Well concerned how to craft it, they never outlined its purpose. 

That purpose was hidden, but you have discovered it. The purpose of the Soulwell is to drink the souls. Each soul nourishes you, transferring their lifespan to you, that remained from the ppoint of death. Sustaining bodily harm will consume a soul to regenerate, with more grievous bodily harm consuming more souls. The drinker can only hold 13 souls at a time.

options.label: Body Snatcher
options.description:
The art of severing your soul from your body and sending it to inhabit the body of another by dislodging the owner's spirit. This technique will allow you to change your identity as frequently as you wish, even evade any paladins that pursue you. Mastering this ritual can allow it to be used on the fly, but failure to perform it correctly will have the most dire consequences. 

Be careful to keep your identity intact, some have gone may from too many snatches and lost their sense of self.

options.label: Körperlos
options.description:
Traditionally preceded by a ritual suicide is the spellbound ritual for freeing the spirit in a ghostly afterlife. 

This spell allows you to free your spirit from its earthly shackles and life in the physical realm as a boundless spirit, with luck allowing the caster to continue interacting with solid objects.

Barrier of wood and stone and the like have no effect upon your new form and though you have forsaken all physical pleasures, no ailment or injury may effect you.

subcategories.name: Kroveri Hæma
subcategories.text: Elvish script inked in human blood and bound in ornate wood, the grimoire radiates a lust for blood. The book itself is addictive, with readers longing to read it more. Those that do master it will be mastered.

subcategories.name: Tier 4
subcategories.text: These are the staple skills of any necromancer

options.label: Create Thrall
options.description: When a person drinks the caster's blood laced with this spell, they will be gifted with the ability to perform superhuman feats for a limited time. If the person drinks this blood 3 times, they shall enter into the caster's service as a thrall, a mindless quasi-vampire with pale skin. They look human, but may only obey the caster's commands, not think.

options.label: Ritual Enhancement
options.description:
By replacing regular paint with blood, usually a pint's worth, you may increase the potency of another ritual or spell that you cast.

This burns out after one use, though it iproves the results of the spell or ritual by 10%.

Doubling the amount of blood used to enhance will grant another 10% bonus.

options.label: Blood Pact
options.description:
A ritual that when performed will cause two people to be bound together by the strength of their word, forcing them to honor fully the pact they made. 

This binding will inflict severe agony or even death upon either one person, or both of the people: If they break their oath, both people will be unable to forget the pact until it is completed.

options.label: Blood Boil
options.description:
A spell that when cast upon a target causes their blood to boil in their veins, elevating their body temperature from 37 degrees to 45 degrees without killing them.

The process is excruciatingly painful and causes harm to both their circulatory system and organs, but any and all damage is undone when the spell is ended.

options.label: Sanguine Senses
options.description:
One spell from the Kroveri Hæma that vastly improves the sensory perception of the one it is cast upon. 

Able to see in pitch-black darkness, smell scents better than a bloodhound, and can hear a pin drop in another room. Vibrations and changes in air pressure can also be easily felt, with earthquakes, storms or other movement audible.

options.label: Lift Bloodstain
options.description: Blood is a precious commodity, and being able to use that which has been wasted, but not used as paint in rituals. This spell allows you to lift blood out of objects, clothes or any other material and send it into a container or flask. Blood that has been lifted from a stain leaves no trace of the stain, nor does it carry with it any traces or contaminants.

subcategories.name: Tier 3
subcategories.text: These skills are a necromancer's main skills.

options.label: Create Nosferatu
options.description:
A beastly drinker of blood, its humanoid visage is marred by the gaunt face, lanky limbs, and bald head. Looking like living corpses, Nosferatu are perverted simulacra of their original race. 

Their claws are sharp and ears pointed, and they have acute senses, great strength and speed. Nosferatu will due when the Mother's light shines upon them.

options.label: Bloody Memories
options.description: A spell cast over blood, either spilt or not, that is then consumed or touched. Touching the blood will allow the caster to experience the last few minutes of a person's life before the blood was shed. Consuming the blood will allow the caster to see the memories of the blood's owner. This requires a ritual to ensure your memories do not mix.

options.label: Blood Spilt Anew
options.description:
Typically used to investigate murders that have no suspects nor victims, this spell enchants a bloodstained object used to commit a murder.

When held near the murderer the blood on the object will flow from the stain. The effect of the spell is visible to all, and is near flawless in its role.

options.label: Bloodthirsty Weapon
options.description: This spell ensorcells a weapon to be sharper and harder to break, with the wielder gaining skill with the weapon. There is a side-effect to this, with the weapon seemingly taking on a life of its own. The wielder will be tempted to draw it more often, and be less willing to grant clemency to opponents.

options.label: Blood Whip
options.description:
The caster of this spell causes blood, either their own blood or blood that is free a body, to leap to their hands and form into a whip-like shape.

This whip feels as solid as a leather whip and grips just as well. 

If the caster ensnares a target in the whip, they may drain the target's blood through the whip.

options.label: Blood Tracking
options.description:
Using a small amount of blood from a target, the caster can use this spell to locate the target. Contained in a wide-bottomed flask or container, the ensorcelled blood will pool in the direction of the target. 

If the ensorcelled blood is dripped upon a map, it will stream to and pool above the target's location, but not soak in.

subcategories.name: Tier 2
subcategories.text: These are the best skills that a necromancer has learnt.

options.label: Night Falls
options.description: The Kroveri Hæma contains a ritual that uses blood-powered spell to bring about night when there was once day. For the next 48 hours, the world is veiled from Mother's light, for as long as you live. The moon shines a blood-red and all natural light is darkened, with only magelight and fire illuminating the world in the darkness.

options.label: River of Blood
options.description: Cast over a source of water such as a river or well, this spell causes the water to turn to blood, rendering it undrinkable to the majority of people. While the blood does not sustain a vampire, it does not coagulate and will those that drink it to become highly suggestible to the caster of the spell.

options.label: Blood Burst
options.description:
A spell in the Kroveri Hæma intended for combat: When cast, it will cause the veins of the target to burst, the blood flying in heavy spurts from their arteries. The target will die, depending on the amount of blood loss suffered. 

The caster can choose the number of veins and arteries that will burst.

options.label: Blood Missile
options.description:
A spell that causes blood to shoot from the caster's hand, vein, or other point of their body. The blood is formed into a missile and is directed by the caster's mind towards a target. 

When the missile hits the target, it hits with force of an arrow, penetrating armor and flesh, leaving only a wound behind instead of a physical object.

options.label: Empower Bloodline
options.description:
There exists, in the Kroveri Hæma, a ritual that will grant a person a single great gift,  which can be performed on another.

Improved intellect, enhanced endurance, hurried healing, any many others may be granted. A single bloodline may only stand to be empowered once. All royalty is Empowered, as is any new monarch.

options.label: Bloodguard
options.description:
This ritual uses blood that is painted upon a body with specific pattern to grant an enhanced resistance to spells. There is another specific pattern that will instead grant enhanced resistance to physical damage. 

The marks upon the body will wash off or be disfigured: To remove the marks requires the wearer to remove them.

subcategories.name: Tier 1
subcategories.text:
In pursuit of immortality, the necromancer has mastered this.

Pick 1 spell from this tier.

options.label: Vampirism
options.description: You read that Empower Bloodline is said to work on one's own bloodline, though the results were never stated. You died. Then you un-died. Now, you are stronger than any living person with an empowered bloodline, stronger, faster, and hardier. You may pass this power on by causing your blood to be drunk by someone. Beware the sun, for the Mother's light burns those that have forsaken her. You require hours of sleep in a coffin each day, or you feel weak.

options.label: Blood Bath
options.description:
While a duchess in a far-off corner of Teb'Hai was condemned to death for daring to use this ritual to preserve her life, if conducted without arousing suspicion, it will indeed provide the results she pursued. 

Bathing in blood will indeed do such things, provided the correct rituals and spells are observed. While not making the ritualist more resistant to damage, they are entirely human and as such lack any physical signs of inhumanity.

subcategories.name: Promræn Caro
subcategories.text: Bound in leather made from human skin and containing parchment pages of human flesh, this grimoire contains the forbidden knowledge to shape and warp flesh. Some secrets may even lead to the creation of life.

subcategories.name: Tier 4
subcategories.text: These are the staple skills of any necromancer.

options.label: Gentle Repose
options.description:
A spell from the early chapter of the Promræn Caro that allows the caster to halt the decay of a body that was caused by death. As long as the spell is active the body will remain exactly as it was when the spell was cast.

This applies to parts of the body that are no longer connected, such as limbs that have been severed.

options.label: Cure Disease
options.description:
Able to kill diseases and purge poisons that reside in, or have been introduced to, people. 

Able to undo the damage caused by diseases, such as necrosis or nerve damage or even coagulated blood. However, this spell cannot reverse death nor undo loss of limbs.

options.label: Cure Injury
options.description: From the Promræn Caro chapter that concerns healing, this spell allows the caster to repair any wound and stem all bleeding. This spell may heal injuries that linger or did not correctly heal. This spell is not able to re-attach limbs nor reverse death, instead focus is placed on such measures not being necessary.

options.label: Create Ghoul
options.description: An individual twisted through a ritual found in the Promræn Caro, a perverted mockery of its former self, the spells used to create the ghoul have robbed it of all memory and identity, leaving it a slave to their creator. It now possesses greater strength, speed, and reflexes but is no more intelligent than a hound. The ghoul may carry out simple commands.

options.label: Reinforcement
options.description: From the Promræn Caro, concerning health, this spell causes the target's bones to increase in strength, even to the point that they may not be broken. Muscles may also be reinforced, lending supernatural strength and reflexes to the target. Their skin when reinforced will turn blades and deflect arrows. Other reinforcements are also mentioned.

options.label: Inflict Paralysis
options.description: A spell that will cause the target to lose the ability to move their extremities as well as muscles and organ able to become paralyzed. Particular limbs or organs can be affected or all of them. The paralysis may slowly affect the target over time, or instantly affect them when the spell is cast.

subcategories.name: Tier 3
subcategories.text: These skills are a necromancer's main skills.

options.label: Warp Flesh
options.description: Spells from the Promræn Caro that allow the caster to twist and shape flesh as if it were clay. Seamlessly attaching flesh and limbs and allowing the new owner to manipulate them as if they were their own. The limbs may have been severed, and when warped will be returned to its original state. The flesh need not be from the host's race.

options.label: Alter Age
options.description: From the Promræn Caro, this spell allows the caster to age a target by any number of years, but no more than 10 years initially. It can age a target or reverse aging, as the caster wishes. Suffering from diminishing returns, the spell's effect will halve each time it is cast on a target, past the initial casting.

options.label: Natural Weapon
options.description: The spell causes the target to grow spines, claws, or other lethal features from their body. The weapons may vary in size and may be composed of any number of things, from bone, skin, muscle, or may even cause the growth of venom sacs and the fangs to use them. An example of weapons that this spell causes is poisonous sweat.

options.label: Create Abomination
options.description:
Outlined in the Promræn Caro are rituals that can cause the horrific mutations of living things into a usually mindless form that possesses great strength and can shrug off most assaults with its giant size. 

Totally obedient to their creator, these abominations will carry out any and all orders they receive.

options.label: Alter Appearance
options.description:
A spell of cosmetic origin that is usually used to disguise the caster. It can alter many aspect of the caster's visage, and even be cast upon another.

The target is changed to resemble that which the caster desires, from a new face to a different body type, to even an entirely different gender.

options.label: Fleshpoint
options.description:
This spell allows the caster to move themselves and others they touch between two points when they touch the points. These points are floating flesh ritually contained within a seal. 

Each seal has a separate string of glyphs that sets its apart from others like it, which lets the caster pinpoint which fleshpoint they wish to teleport.

subcategories.name: Tier 2
subcategories.text: These are the best skills that a necromancer has learnt.

options.label: Create Life
options.description:
Requiring a sample of a person be placed inside a metal barrel engraved with spells form the Promræn Caro.

An ignition spell from the Promræn Caro will transform the sample into a rapidly growing embryo. The grown life's age is determined by the size of the barrel, larger for older. It will take on the sample donor's visage, sans memory.

options.label: Create Skinwalker
options.description:
Taking a human and binding them, spells are cast over them and their body contorted. They gain the strength, speed, and endurance of two men. They must wear a sentient person's skin, taking on their likeness.

They may also perfectly mimic any voice they hear. The skinwalker's intelligence is lowered, slowly returning over time.

options.label: Mass Growth
options.description:
The Promræn Caro has within it a spell that will cause flora to take on a life of its own, causing tentacles to grow as well as massive increases in size. 

The flora becomes almost animal-like, with fast reflexes that can strike out at enemies. 

These plants are loyal to their creator, and can be controlled mentally.

options.label: Wereform
options.description: In the Promræn Caro there is a chapter that illustrates a person changing into a beastly figure. It lists the spells and rituals that will allow the caster to change a person into a being that can take on the traits of an animal. Requiring a sample of the animal to be enchanted and then used to lightly injure the target, they will change under the moon's light.

options.label: Create Fleshpoint
options.description:
This ritual allows the caster to create a fleshpoint binding two or more points together, or adding to an established fleshpoint network. 

The fleshpoint can be any sizable piece of flesh, such as an arm, finger, or even a head. The glyphs require a unique combination with one serving as the point of origin to function.

options.label: Craft Plague
options.description:
A spell that cause a sample of blood or an existing disease to mutate into one that carries the traits desired. 

The plague may be transmitted however you wish and even target only specific kinds of people, and may be benevolent or malevolent, grant enhanced strength or cause atrophy.

One with Cure Disease may cure it.

options.label: Devourer
options.description: By following the steps laid out in a ritual in the Promræn Caro, your physical form underwent a series of changes that grant immortality. By consuming the healthy flesh and working organs of the living, yours are replaced, extending your life. Any parts of a foreign race that offer performance superior to your own can be consumed. While physical damage may kill you, consuming flesh will regenerate you. An innate ability to know which parts need replacing comes with the ritual.

options.label: Potion of Khizaz
options.description: The Promræn Caro contains a formula tied with a ritual that details a method to restore the body and reverse aging. This method results in a potion that will alter the very fundamental function of the physical body. By adding a small vial of one's own blood to this potion, it takes on a greenish hue, and begins to crystalize and harden. This crystal is swallowed, and soon your age will be reversed. Any missing parts will regrow this once, and you will be permanently youthful though mortal by any means.

options.label: Alpha Skinwalker
options.description: Skinwalkers are great mimics but their pretense of humanity is a charade that does not convince for long. Another ritual found, in the same chapter as the skinwalker spells, will allow you to transform yourself into a skinwalker, able to mimic any person you hear, and wear their skin to appear as the person. Your strength, speed, and endurance as well as your intelligence remain unaffected by your transformation, and you can sustain more damage than a regular mortal.

subcategories.name: Reunu Pertemru
subcategories.text: The Reunu Pertemru is the first of all necromantic works, containing many ancient secrets in the form of a scroll. The ability to cast curses has since been lost, and other esoteric enigmas remain hidden, perhaps rightly so.

subcategories.name: Tier 4
subcategories.text: These are the staple skills of any necromancer.

options.label: Sand Storm
options.description:
Spells that exert control over sand and direct it to the caster's will.

The ability to control sound we against the more sand that is affected, as well as the further the castor is from the sand. The caster may craft weapons or a small objects from sand or even direct a sandstorm up to a kilometer wide, or any action in between.

options.label: Emblaming
options.description:
Ritually cast, this spell causes the targeted  corpse to dry up and become immune to decay. The spell permeates the corpse and shields it from natural consequences of death, preserving it for an indefinite period of time. 

After permeating the corpse the spell causes it to harden and become very resistant to damage.

options.label: Curse of Aging
options.description:
Magic cast that can be triggered by a trap or door opening, or regular casting. Either instantly or after a delay the target will age until they are elderly. 

They will suffer all the symptoms and ills of old age, though they will still be as youthful as they were before the curse. The natural lifespan will ont change but the target will be affected by infirmity.

options.label: Create mummy
options.description: The ritual which a deceased person is mummified, with their internal organs removed and spells cast over them. This bestows great power, a hardier form that is more resistant to damage, and a weakened version of your curses. These mummies are loyal servants that carry out every command of the one who created them.

options.label: Curse of Enfeeblement
options.description: Magic cast that can be triggered by a trap or door opening, or regular casting. Either immediately or after a delay, the target will begin to feel weak, their limbs heavy, and they will be compelled to sleep. Upon waking, they will be killed with lethargy. They will no longer be as strong and fit as they once were, instead they will be as brawny as an elderly man.

options.label: Curse of Pain
options.description: This curse causes the target to lose the ability to distinguish between the two extremes of sensory perceptions. Pleasurable sensations will be caused to feel as painful as torture, and any painful sensation will feel like ecstasy. The result of this is a painful pleasure. This effect may be gradually applied or in an instant.

subcategories.name: Tier 3
subcategories.text: These skills are a necromancer's main skills.

options.label: Curse of Deprivation
options.description: Magic cast that can be triggered by a trap or door opening, or regular casting. Targets will over time begin to become unable to use their senses, with even the sensation of touch not unaffected. The senses affected and the degree to which they are affected is determined by the caster. The caster may also choose if the victim senses the caster.

options.label: Curse of Disquiet
options.description: Magic cast that can be triggered by a trap or door opening, or regular casting. The target will noto immediately begin to be affected, though overtime a feeling of unease and distress will accumulate, causing the target to develop severe anxiety and even insomnia, with daily life becoming uncomfortable. Eventually, a feeling of impending doom will occur.

options.label: Curse of Hallucination
options.description: Magic cast that can be triggered by a trap or door opening, or regular casting. After triggering, either immediately or after a delay, the target will experience hallucinations that are indistinguishable from reality. These hallucinations will to the target appear to be able to move objects or harm the target; though it is all imagined.

options.label: Curse of Suffering
options.description:
Magic cast that can be triggered by a trap or door opening, or regular casting. Those affected will either isntantly or over time begin to feel pain and even agony, as if their entire body was on fire and every bone broken. 

While no harm will actually be caused, the anguish experienced will feel real.

options.label: Curse of Chains
options.description:
Magic cast that can be triggered by a trap or door opening, or regular casting. From all dark and shadowy corners emerge dozens of hooked chains that ensnare the target, piercing their flesh and pulling it tight.

Controlled mentally by the caster, the chains can lift the target or even tear them apart.

options.label: Schmerz Rätsel
options.description:
This ritual allows you to construct a small puzzle-box. This is bound to the creator and serves as an indestructible key to the Domun Lacrimans. 

The Schmerz Rätsel allows the creator to abduct the solver back to their Domun Lacrimans. After this, the box will return to its original configuration.

options.label: Create Eremite
options.description: The ritual by which a lesser Eremite being is crafted from one of the mortal races. They will undergo scarification, be clad in leather and experience a number of horrific and tortorous acts in their transformation. The Eremite will be subservient to the caster, and share in their powers. The suffering of others will nourish and sustain them.

options.label: Regeneration
options.description:
Restoring the body back to its original state by stealing the health and life force of others, leaving them a husk. This skill allows the caster to recover from almost any injury as long as there is a good supply of people to drain. 

While it heals damage and replaces lost organs and body parts, it does nothing to reverse aging.

options.label: Domun Lacrimans
options.description:
This spell creates for you a small pocket dimension: 100 meters cubed. 

It is formed from metal and stone, filled with shadow, with hooks and chains that hand from the ceiling. 

After the spell's resolution, you will be transported inside: The only way in or out is your Schmerz Rätsel being solved.

options.label: Resurrection
options.description: The ability to bring the dead back to life with a spell in the Reunu Pertemru, they look exactly as they did before they were raised. Consisting of calling the spirit of the deceased back to inhabit their body once again, it works best on willing souls, but can be applied as well upon reluctant individuals.

options.label: Curse of Death
options.description: Magic cast that can be triggered by a trap or door opening, or regular casting. Depending upon the chosen time of the caster, the affect of this curse may cause the death of the affected instantly or delayed until a later time. The manner of death may also be chosen when casting it, though deaths necessitating an external force may not be cast.

options.label: Scourge of Scarabs
options.description:
This spell calls forth a swarm of scarabs that burrow into the flesh of the living people, inflicting suffering upon them while moving towards their brain. 

Once here, the scarab lodges itself in the part that controls motor movements and takes over the body. These scarabs are under the command of the caster and carry out their desires.

subcategories.name: Tier 1
subcategories.text:
In pursuit of immortality the necromancer has mastered this. 

Pick 1 spell from this tier.

options.label: Mummification
options.description:
Your research into the ancient texts from Teb'lhr have come to fruition with your discovery of mummification. Requiring that your minions and any companions finish the ritual you start, you end your life and your minions inter your body. With the desiccated and bandaged corpse rising from its stone sarcophagus you live again. This form is resilient and can withstand most forms of physical assault. 

Despite not being a lich, mummies still have a phylactery: Their bodies.

options.label: Worm that walks
options.description:
The Homme-Da was a most horrific punishment reserved for those that have committed the most heinous treason, with carnivorous worms eating their flesh until they died. 

This method of execution is painful, but anyone awoken from this death will become a plague, almost immune to physical damage, and able to regenerate from damage. Individual worms can be used as scouts but when returned share their new knowledge through their very limited senses.

options.label: Eremite
options.description:
To become an Eremite, one requires a secret and forbidden spell, one that will tear your soul apart. Clad tight in leather, mutilated beyond recognition, Eremites are no longer able to be considered mortal.

Mastery over suffering is the hallmark of the Eremite and you shall have it. 

Eremites are immortal and difficult to harm due to the suffering of others nourishing and sustaining them.

subcategories.name: Items
subcategories.text:
Pick 3 items. 

Some are required for immortalities.

options.label: Schmerz Rätsel
options.description:
You crafted this puzzle-box by hand from expensive materials and it is nearly indestructible. 

It serves as a key for your Domum Lacrimas, and as a conduit for your curses.

It takes hours to solve, even for you.

options.label: Liber Necromos
options.description:
A grimoire filled in a little bookshop in a city that you once visited and purchased. For some reason, after you got it home, it began talking to you, whispering secrets in your ear, and giving you rituals and spells that you have never seen before.

Ph'nglui mglw'nafh Abholoth
H'Nall wgah nagl fhtagn

options.label: Phylactery
options.description:
The key to immortality.

Crafted by those that wish to transform into liches, it is usually a very expensive object that is enchanted  to become a phylactery. 

The spells and rituals used improve its durability and make it near-indestructible.

options.label: Hand of Glory
options.description:
The pickled left hand of one that was hanged, this candle-holder has special powers.

When used in a ritual or when casting a spell, will bind the ritual or spell's duration to the life of the candle. 

The hand grants protection to this candle, shielding it from damage or removal.

options.label: Small Fortune
options.description: From a rich family, or just really lucky, there is a small fortune in gold that belongs to you. There are no strings and no catch to this so you can live comfortably, wating for nothing, provided you do not get caught doing anything heretical.

options.label: Vial of Blood
options.description:
An enchanted antique glass container filled with blood. 

It may fuel spells as a replacement for the caster's blood as a cost, or be shaped or be used as material for a spell or crafted into a weapon. The vial can be emptied or used for any other purpose.

options.label: Coffin
options.description:
Used in the funerary rites of the Mother's followers, this holds a body comfortably.

Vampires use these as their resting places in the daytime to retain their strength.

options.label: Xanthuun Vat
options.description: Made from expensively-made curved glass inscribed with symbols from the Promræn Caro, this machine is used to grow life from a donor sample. They come in various sizes to grow people to various ages.

options.label: Horn of the Dead
options.description: Carved from the horn of a long dead beast and inscribed with runes of power, it has the power to command the dead.By blowing into it, the user can use chord progressions to give orders to the dead, whether or not they have any power.

options.label: Haunted Sword
options.description: Inhabited by the spirit of a dead soldier, it houses their soul and mind and allows them to communicate with, and even control the body of, the wielder. The sword grants martial skill to the wielder, equal to the level of the soul housed inside.

options.label: Necromantic Staff
options.description: Skulls and bones bound to a shaft, possessing it, granting the wielder the combined wisdom of all four of the spirits. Amplifying the wielder's power, the range and duration fo all spells and curses as well as undead command is increased.

options.label: Soul Well
options.description: Made to hold the souls of sentient beings, its size determined by its maker. It is located carefully and bound to them eternally.

options.label: Mother's Light
options.description:
One of a series of holy relics made to repel, or maybe even unbind, the undead. 

Able to be mounted upon a staff, when activated by the earnest belief of a follower all dead within a 20m radius will be repelled and unable to enter.

options.label: Spirit Vesel
options.description: Freshly dead, drugged and unwilling or lab-grow, this is a body intended to be used as a vessel in a spirit transfer ritual. It is not restricted to a single gender or even the gender of the caster, allowing for identity changes if they are desired.

subcategories.name: Clothes
subcategories.text: Pick 1

options.label: Common Clothes
options.description:
Plain and well-made, warm, and conservative: These clothes allow the wearer to blend in with the common folk. 

No outstanding designs or anything to catch the eye, these are perfect for one that wishes to remain unnoticed.

The wearer garners no additional respect for wearing these as they would when wearing Aristocratic Clothing.

options.label: Aristocrat Clothes
options.description: Worn by merchants, dukes, counts, and barons as well as princes and queens, these clothes are finely stitched and embroidered but not very warm or protective. Silks and other quality cloth were used in their design and creation and these clothes shout richness and wealth for all to see. These clothes are made to look good.

options.label: Stealthy Clothes
options.description:
From leather clothes to a religious raiment and anything inbetween, they act as a costume or tactical gear that lets you blend in with crowds, slip by unnoticed or anything else that is desired.

With varying degrees of protection, it is best to choose the rest kind of garb. 

The most these clothes can offer is light protection.

options.label: Suit of Armor
options.description:
Crafted from strongly-linked chainmail, masterfully crafted plate with a central religious icon, this suit of armor offers excellent protection from melee weapons without a significant loss in mobility. 

Lightweight with few chinks to exploit, the wearer will have the appearance of a knight in shining armor, not a brigand burglar or even a commoner.

options.label: Mage Clothes
options.description:
Impressive in appearance and striking in style, there are many hidden pockets within the robes but out of view. 

Not very protective, excellently insulated, they are great in heat and the cold. 

They are available in unique versions to match all the schools of necromancy, as well as other schools of magic if the wearer wishes to be discreet.

options.label: Holy Clothes
options.description:
The garb chosen by the priests and priestesses of the Mother: It is white which represents her light. Wearers of the holy garb are respected everywhere and well-known for their ability to heal and comfort the injured and sick. All wearers have this reputation, whether they have earnt it or not. 

Even ne'er-do-wells respect this authority.

options.label: Sinti Clothes
options.description:
The traditional style of dress for the nomadic people known as the Sinti. Flashy and gaudy in color, they are eye-catching and not very practical.

They insulate very well and work best in heat, such as the desert, with their combination of tight and baggy parts. 

The wearer attracts the stigma of the traveling life, and may be looked down upon by the people.

options.label: Adapted Clothes
options.description:
Typically worn by foreigners in foreign lands, these clothes are different than what is normally worn, and fir better with the environment. Chosen to fit a particular need or niche, they may also help the wearer blend in to a group or civilization that may not be as welcoming. 

Colors and styles usually depend on the region, but they all match the locale.

subcategories.name: Modifiers
subcategories.text: Pick 2 companions

options.label: Studious (Spell)
options.description: You may pick 1 less companions and receive +1 spell

options.label: Studious (Item)
options.description: You may pick 1 less companions and receive +1 item

options.label: Socialite (spell)
options.description: You may pick 1 more companionbut receive -1 spell

options.label: Socialite (item)
options.description: You may pick 1 more companionbut receive -1 item

options.label: Sarah
options.description:
A young woman with a remarkable skill at hæmomancy. She knows many tricks and secrets and can aid you well. Her ability to control and manipulate blood is unmatched. 

"See here, how I flick my wrist? This is how you whip with blood."

options.label: Lady Aino
options.description:
The Red Lady is an old countess with a talent for hæmomancy. She has established herself as a land owner that dominates the region, and will not be willing to move much. 

"The world would be so boring without idiots like you to amuse me."

options.label: Kaija
options.description:
An imprisoned vampire, held deep within a stronghold. She is starving and weak, but if you free her will become your loyal ally. When fed, she is remarkably strong and swift. 

"I've been hungry for so long, but you are going to help me change that."

options.label: Eka
options.description:
A vampire in the shape of a young girl: She has a hidden brutality. Ela claims you as her own, making you do as she says. Her strength is much more than her size would indicate. 

"Now... it is time to play."

options.label: Nazar
options.description:
A painter with a thirst for pain: He has a great knowledge of anatomy and he is willing to teach you all of his arts. Despite living a hedonistic life, he is still a formidable fighter. 

"Now, it is time for us to start dealing with the business at hand."

options.label: General Makari
options.description:
Once the head of the vampire army that was defeated millennia ago. He wishes to make up for his failure to win a decisive battle, and sees a partnership making that happen. 

"Together we will slaughter them all! Amenthes will not get in my way again."

options.label: Lester
options.description:
A socialite vampire with a taste for high society, he has homes in the major cities, but no real friends. He desires a companion to share his unlife, and enjoy it with him.

"Yes... excellent! I have not had this much fin in ages!"

options.label: Baron Orloke
options.description:
The baron has gret strength and a mind that belies his appearance. He has had few friends and is visage scares most. His castle retains a library with books on many things. 

"You stand before me... I am impressed."

options.label: Nadya
options.description:
A spirit bound to the Liber Animas, serving without end. Once a young servant girl, her life was prematurely taken. She is a good person that does not like doing bad things. 

"Turning to mage 487. Regarding the soul..."

options.label: Grace
options.description:
The unlucky spirit of a woman, she has ben alone for years. Not many have seen her so she has decided to latch onto you. She will make herself useful despite having no magic. 

"Hey listen, I recognize that place. I get in there for you."

options.label: Cassandra
options.description:
The spirit of a dead necromancer that was set free from her body due to a ritual being interrupted. She cannot do much since then but if you find her a vessel, she will teach you.

"No, no, that's now how you do it... If only I had a body..."

options.label: Morgan
options.description:
Morgan had always been in contact with spirits form a young age, and has grown up knowing how to make them do her bidding. She has no skills to the living though.

"I don't get it, why did he run away when I said I talk to dead people?"

options.label: Kolya
options.description:
An ancient bodysnatcher with many secrets. He has stolen a great many forms, but could not steal a friend. He is very selfish and stubborn but may one day mellow out. 

"Why worry about danger when you can become the danger?"

options.label: Em'Al
options.description:
A human subjected to a cruel fate, their soul bound in a suit of armor. They broke free and have been working to right the wrongs they were forced to commit.

"I only look mean and evil. I used to be a farmer, for Mother's sake!"

options.label: Risdare
options.description:
A mounted warrior and his stead. Killed in combat and somehow returned from the dead. He still has all his skills and his axe remains deadly as it was in life. 

"Do not shy away from the light. Do you want to live forever?"

options.label: Endhinat
options.description:
Ancient and cunning, he is the creator of one of the first soulwells. He estimates more than a thousand souls have passed his lips, but he seeks a protege to teach.

Nothing tastes as sweet as a soul plucked before it is ripened."

options.label: Patchwerk
options.description:
Sewn together from several bodies, she has an eclectic personality, though she is rather vain. 

Her creator taught her necromancy even though she had no aptitude. 

"Do you think I am pretty? I will trade a lesson for a compliment."

options.label: Elizzbeth
options.description:
An eccentric and affluent woman, with no medical license due to some questionable surgeries. Somehow she always makes reattachments work, with neither seams nor scars. 

"What's the problem with giving someone another pair of arms?"

options.label: Libyn
options.description:
An angst-filled woman angry at someone for a reason she will not say. She was originally a sorcerer, but now has the ability to create weapons from her body.

"I will impale them, burn them, make them suffer, then they can die."

options.label: Catherine
options.description:
One of your masters first creations, she is an old friend that has been with you from the beginning. She has learnt much about flesh magic, and from your master.

"You see, this is how you do it. A little more here, some less there..."

options.label: Valaul
options.description:
A creation that was abandoned, he has been alone until you found him. You are his model of behavior. He has skills in fleshcraft and wants to become more like you.

"Will you be my friend? Nobody wants to be my friend."

options.label: Kreie
options.description:
A Kreierung, created in a Xanthuum Vat, they are based on a mix of samples. They will use you as their model of behavior, as they have only known life with you.
